mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Sport SVR engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A reconditioned or rebuilt Range Rover Sport SVR engine typically costs between £9,000 and £18,000 for the supply-only unit, depending on the level of rebuild and specialist documentation provided.
- Rebuilt units include upgraded timing chains and metal tensioners to prevent recurrence.
- Supply and fit packages are available through our premium specialist network.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Range Rover Sport SVR?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Early detection is critical to preventing catastrophic damage to your Range Rover Sport SVR engine.
- Listen for a distinct rattling or ticking noise from the front of the engine, especially during a cold start.
- Look for check engine lights, loss of power, or metal flakes in the oil filter during servicing.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Sport SVR?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, given the strong retained values of the SVR, replacing the engine is a highly sound financial decision.
- A typical 2015-2022 SVR is valued between £45,000 and £85,000+, making a £12,000-£18,000 rebuild a small percentage of the vehicle's worth.
- A rebuilt engine with a 12-month warranty adds reliability and protects your premium performance asset.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Sport SVR engine supply and fit take?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A straightforward supply and fit replacement for a Range Rover Sport SVR typically takes 4 to 6 days at a premium specialist workshop.
- This allows time for the engine to be delivered, mounted, and thoroughly calibrated and tested.
- Complex cases requiring additional cooling system or supercharger upgrades may take slightly longer.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my Range Rover Sport to an SVR engine?

acceptedAnswer.text:
While both use the AJ133 architecture, a direct swap is not straightforward.
- The SVR AJ133S requires different ECU mapping, supercharger calibration, exhaust system, and cooling upgrades to function correctly and pass MOT.
- We strongly recommend sticking to a like-for-like AJ133S replacement to ensure guaranteed compatibility, reliability, and warranty coverage.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover Sport SVR - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the SVR (Special Vehicle Racing) badge was introduced to the Range Rover Sport lineup, it represented the pinnacle of JLR performance engineering, pairing a 5.0-litre supercharged V8 with enhanced dynamics and exclusive styling to create the fastest and most powerful Sport ever built.

milestones.description: AJ133S (4999cc), 567hp, launched with the L494 Range Rover Sport SVR, featuring an uprated version of the AJ133 supercharged V8 with revised supercharger calibration and performance exhaust.
Minor calibration updates and Carbon Edition special variant introduced, maintaining the same 567hp output with enhanced interior and exterior specifications.
Final year of L494 SVR production, replaced by the L461 generation with different powertrain options (P530 BMW V8).

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Sport SVR Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Sport SVR features a highly refined 5.0-litre supercharged V8 engine. While mechanically robust, the high-stress performance application and complex supercharger system require specialist attention. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Range Rover Sport SVR AJ133S Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: Plastic timing chain tensioners degrade and lose hydraulic pressure under the high-stress performance driving typical of SVR owners, allowing chain slack. If ignored, the chain can skip teeth on camshaft sprockets, causing valves to contact pistons - catastrophic engine failure requiring full replacement.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chains, upgraded metal tensioners, guides, and VVT hardware before failure occurs.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable only if caught early (audible rattle but no running issues); upgraded metal tensioners prevent recurrence.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing chains and metal tensioners, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has already jumped or engine has suffered valve damage.

problems.recommendation: If your SVR has a full service history and the timing chain rattle is caught early, invest in the preventative chain replacement immediately - it will be the best £2,500-£4,000 you spend on this vehicle. However, if the engine has already jumped timing, developed a knock, or is burning significant oil (80k+ miles), a full reconditioned replacement with upgraded tensioners and oil control components is the only safe path. Do not risk a used AJ133S - many carry the same tensioner weakness.

problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Supercharger Seal Leaks - Why the Range Rover Sport SVR AJ133S Requires Attention
problems.rootCause: The AJ133S burns oil at a rate of up to 1 litre per 1,000 miles due to cylinder bore glazing and valve stem seal wear, exacerbated by the high-stress supercharged application. The supercharger nose seal can fail, allowing oil to leak onto belts. If oil levels are not meticulously maintained, spun rod bearings and bottom-end failure follow.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Oil analysis, PCV valve replacement, switch to high-performance 5W-50 oil, regular level monitoring, supercharger seal replacement.
repairOptions.longevity: Ongoing management; does not fix root cause but can extend engine life if oil never runs low.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded oil control components and resealed supercharger, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The permanent fix for high-mileage SVRs with advanced oil burning.
